title: Tate residue calculus for a discrete valuation subalgebra
statement:
Let $k\subset K$ be fields and $O\subset K$ a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] containing $k$, with fraction field $K$ and residue field $\kappa=O/\mathfrak m$ finite over $k$. For every $f\in K$ the quotient $(fO+O)/O$ is finite-dimensional over $k$. Choose a $k$-linear projection $\pi:K\to O$ whose restriction to $O$ is the identity. A $k$-linear endomorphism $T$ of a $k$-vector space $W$ is finite-potent if $T^N(W)$ is finite-dimensional for some integer $N\ge1$; for such $T$, define $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}(T)$ as the ordinary trace of $T$ on any finite-dimensional $T$-stable subspace of $W$ containing $T^N(W)$, which does not depend on $N$ or on the subspace. For $f,g\in K$ the commutator below is a finite-potent endomorphism of $W=K$. The rule
$$\operatorname{res}_O(f\,dg)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{fp}}\bigl([\pi\circ m_f,m_g]\bigr),\qquad m_f(a)=fa,\quad [A,B]=AB-BA,$$
extends to a $k$-linear map $\Omega^1_{K/k}\to k$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], independent of $\pi$ and of the finite-dimensional subspace in the trace. It annihilates the image of $\Omega^1_{O/k}$ in $\Omega^1_{K/k}$. For a uniformizer $t\in O$ and $u\in O$ it satisfies
$$\operatorname{res}_O(u\,t^{-1}dt)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa/k}(\bar u).$$
If $\kappa/k$ is separable, a $k$-algebra coefficient-field identification $\widehat O\cong\kappa[[t]]$ exists, and for the image $\sum_{m\gg-\infty}a_m t^m dt$ of any $\xi\in\Omega^1_{K/k}$ in continuous differentials of $\kappa((t))/k$ one has
$$\operatorname{res}_O(\xi)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa/k}(a_{-1}).$$
